Read the package documentation

One chart for every bitbaum product. A line, ranked bars, a share bar, a sparkline, a meter, a timeline and a strip of figures — drawn on the server from the app's own tokens, each with a table behind it and no label that clips, overlaps or shrinks — so a fix made once reaches every product.

Why it exists: on 2026-10-23 the owner said visualisations are "super important", a profile must be "more useful than Bloomberg", and "it's packages what makes us special". Substrata had one hand-rolled line chart and nothing else; every other product had none. This is the one place charts now live. (Colour and type come from design-tokens; chartkit is the drawing.)

Install

pnpm add @bitbaum/chartkit@^0.3.0

Install releases from npm, never a commit or a branch, for the reason chatkit's README gives: a semver range is what lets a fix reach every product.

Use

import { LineChart, BarChart, ColumnChart, ShareBars, Sparkline, Meter, Timeline, StatTiles } from "@bitbaum/chartkit/react";
import "@bitbaum/chartkit/styles.css";

<LineChart
  series={[{ id: "backlog", label: "Backlog", points: [{ x: "2025-Q1", y: 29, href: "…" }] }]}
  unit="GW"
  caption="GE Vernova Gas Power equipment backlog, GW, by quarter."
  yFrom="zero"                       // or "data"; left out, zero only when the data sits near it
  height={208}                       // CSS px; the width is the container's
/>
<LineChart                           // a year of daily closes: a clean line with a light fill
  series={[{ id: "close", label: "Close", points: closes }]}
  unit="USD"
  yFrom="data"
  markers="auto"                     // "all" (default) | "none" | "ends" | "auto"
  area                               // faint fill under the line, in the series' token colour
  caption="NVIDIA daily closes, USD, last 12 months."
/>
<BarChart rows={[{ label: "China", value: 900000, share: 0.99, estimated: true }, { label: "Other", value: null }]} unit="kg" caption="…" highlight="China" />
<ShareBars rows={[{ label: "BlackRock", share: 0.074 }]} other={0.926} otherLabel="Others, each below 5%" caption="…" />
<ColumnChart series={[{ id: "rev", label: "Revenue", points: [{ x: "FY2024", y: 61 }, { x: "FY2025", y: -4, href: "…" }] }]} unit="USD bn" caption="…" />
<Sparkline points={points} label="Backlog over six quarters" />
<Meter value={12} max={12} label="Severity" href="/methods/severity" />
<Timeline events={[{ date: "2026-07-17", label: "…", tone: "down", href: "…" }]} caption="…" />
<StatTiles tiles={[{ label: "Bottlenecks mapped", value: 33, href: "/bottlenecks" }]} />

x is an ISO period (2025, 2025-Q2, 2025-03, 2025-03-31) or a number. Several series share one axis — there is no second y-axis and never will be; two measures of different scale are two charts. BarChart ranks its rows (largest first, no number last) whatever order they arrive in, draws a null as "—" and an estimate with "≈". ShareBars names its remainder otherLabel (left out, "Other") — say what the rest is, never a bare "Other 87%". ColumnChart draws periods left to right in the order given (fiscal labels are not re-sorted), several series side by side, a loss below the zero line, and a missing figure as no column and "—" in the table. Every point of a LineChart and every event of a Timeline is an anchor when it has an href, with its value, period and note on hover and on keyboard focus.

markers says which values of a LineChart carry a dot: all (the default, as before) every one; none the line alone; ends only each series' last value; auto every one up to 60 points on a series and none above — 250 daily closes drawn as 250 beads is a string of pearls, not a price line. A value whose dot is hidden is still there: its target is a full-height strip of the plot (the strips tile it, so a pointer or a finger anywhere over the line finds the nearest value), and hover or keyboard focus shows its dot, a hairline cursor and the value. The table behind the chart holds every value either way. area adds a light fill under each line in that series' own --ck-series-* colour — never a literal.

What every chart guarantees

  • It renders on the server. Pure SVG and HTML, no effect, no measurement.

The drawing is an SVG stretched to its box (preserveAspectRatio="none", non-scaling strokes); every label is HTML in rem laid over it in per cent, so a 320px plot has the same type as a 1440px one.

  • Nothing is reachable only by pointing. Each chart is a `<figure

class="ck-chart"> with its caption and a visually hidden <table> of the same values; the decorative parts are aria-hidden`, the anchors are not.

  • No label clips or overlaps. Long labels truncate with an ellipsis and

carry the full text in title; bar labels have a least column; timeline events that would collide take a second lane; the y gutter is as wide as its widest number. @bitbaum/chartkit/audit measures it (below).

  • Colour and type come only from --ck-* variables, which default to

design-tokens and can be set once on :root: --ck-ink, --ck-ink-muted, --ck-line, --ck-bg, --ck-accent, --ck-up, --ck-down, --ck-series-1 … -6, --ck-font, --ck-mono. Series are by index, never cycled, and each after the first has a dash as well as a colour, so the set survives a monochrome theme and a print. The prefix is shared with chatkit on purpose: --ck-line, --ck-accent, --ck-bg, --ck-font and --ck-mono mean the same in both, so an app that themed its chat has themed its charts. Light and dark both work by token.

The audit

import { CHART_DEFECTS_SOURCE } from "@bitbaum/chartkit/audit";
const defects = await page.evaluate(`(${CHART_DEFECTS_SOURCE})(document.body)`);
if (defects.length) throw new Error(defects.join("\n"));

findChartDefects(root) runs inside the page and returns every piece of chart text whose box leaves its chart or overlaps another piece of text in the same chart, one line each. Reading the CSS finds none of these; laying the words out with the real font at the real width does. test/browser.mjs runs it over the demo at 320, 390 and 1280px in light and dark, and first over a deliberately broken figure, to prove the gate can fail.

Develop

pnpm install
pnpm run verify       # format:check, lint, typecheck, build, test, test:browser
pnpm run demo         # builds demo/dist; open demo/index.html

test:browser needs Chromium: pnpm exec playwright install chromium, or set CHROMIUM_PATH. dist/ is committed so a github: install needs no build step; pnpm run check:dist says whether it matches the source.

For proportions, pass the whole as max: <BarChart rows={[{ label: "Share", value: 1.6 }]} max={100} unit="%" caption="Share of the whole" /> draws a 1.6% bar. Without max, bars are relative to the largest row. The scale always expands to fit larger values; invalid or non-positive maxima fall back to the largest row. Accessible tables retain the original values.

Changelog and releases

Read the repository changelog

0.3.0

  • LineChart markers — "all" (default, unchanged) | "none" |

"ends" | "auto". auto drops the dots above 60 points on a series, so a year of daily closes reads as a line rather than ~250 beads; ends keeps only each series' last value. Hidden values stay reachable: each is a full-height strip of the plot (the strips tile it edge to edge), and hover or keyboard focus shows its dot, a hairline cursor and its value.

  • LineChart area — a light fill under each line in the series' token

colour (color-mix of --ck-series-*, never a hex).

  • Core: areaPath, hitColumns, resolveMarkers, AUTO_MARKER_LIMIT,

type LineMarkers.

  • Browser check now runs at 1440px too, and checks the dense chart at 390 and

1440px: no dots drawn, strips tile the plot, hover/focus shows the value on screen.

0.2.0

  • ShareBars otherLabel; ColumnChart for values by period.
